datasets.name: Class noise versions of the 9 real-world datasets (e.g. 'aclx=20%', 'aclx=40%'; 18 datasets)
datasets.group: Noisy modified real-world datasets - Class Noise (Table 9)
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Pairwise class noise scheme of [57]: each majority class example has probability x/100 of being incorrectly labeled as minority; x = 20% and x = 40%; applied to each of the 9 real-world datasets (acl from [45], rest KEEL)

datasets.name: Attribute noise versions of the 9 real-world datasets (e.g. 'aclx=20%', 'aclx=40%'; 18 datasets)
datasets.group: Noisy modified real-world datasets - Attribute noise (Table 9)
datasets.how_obtained_detail: Attribute noise scheme of [57]: each attribute Ai corrupted separately; ~x% of examples chosen and Ai set to a uniform random value between domain min and max (numerical) or a random domain value (nominal); x = 20% and x = 40%; applied to each of the 9 real-world datasets

ir_definition: IR = N- / N+, 'the relation between the majority class and minority class examples', where N- and N+ are the number of examples of the majority and minority classes (Eq. 1); imbalanced when IR > 1

chosen.metric: AUC (no G-mean or other metric reported)

win_claim.quote: The results show that the new proposal performs better than existing SMOTE generalizations for all these different scenarios.

notes: Proposed method: SMOTE–IPF (SMOTE followed by Iterative-Partitioning Filter; majority voting, n=9 partitions, k=3, p=1%; SMOTE k=5, HVDM, balance to 50%). Evaluation: 5 runs of stratified 5-fold CV, AUC, C4.5 (main). Other result tables with SMOTE per dataset: Table 3 (30 synthetic, p.11) and Table 9 (36 noisy real-world, class and attribute noise 20%/40%, p.13); Wilcoxon vs SMOTE also in Table 4 (synthetic: R+ 366.0, R- 99.0, p 0.0050) and Table 10 (noisy). Results for k-NN, SVM, RIPPER and PART are only on the web page http://sci2s.ugr.es/noisebor-imbalanced (p.3), not fetched. Implementation in KEEL (www.keel.es). No supplementary file referenced. All tables were extractable as text (is_image=false).
